source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Give a simple advance explanation and use a visual schedule or social story to show what will happen, preserving predictability before care begins today.","B":"Give a detailed verbal explanation after the procedure begins because advance preparation may increase distress when the child's routine is changing.","C":"Use figurative language and indirect hints before the procedure because abstract communication promotes flexibility more effectively than concrete information.","D":"Change the care routine frequently without advance explanation because repeated unexpected changes are the preferred way to reduce distress over time."}}
source_row.rationale: Predictability and concrete preparation can reduce distress for many children with autism. Option A is correct because CDC describes consistency, visual supports, and Social Stories that give simple descriptions of what to expect. Option B delays preparation until after the procedure begins. Option C relies on abstract figurative language rather than concrete information. Option D deliberately increases unexpected change rather than predictability.
source_row.source_detail: CDC — Treatment and Intervention for Autism Spectrum Disorder, developmental/educational supports: many autistic people benefit from consistency, routines that can be written or drawn, pairing verbal instructions with visual supports, and Social Stories that provide simple descriptions of what to expect in a situation. Current CDC autism treatment/intervention guidance live-rechecked 2026-08-15. NCSBN first-check: Client Needs — Psychosocial Integrity: mental-health symptom recognition, therapeutic communication, behavioral adaptation and culturally/person-centered psychosocial support as applicable. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.

source_row.stem: A child with autism spectrum disorder becomes distressed by unexpected procedures. The child needs a blood draw that was not part of the usual routine. Which approach is most appropriate?
